target.title: fix(config): allow case-distinct agent dirs on sensitive volumes
target.body:
Closes #105194

AI-assisted: implementation and review preparation used Codex. I understand the code and verified the filesystem behavior described below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using case-sensitive macOS or Windows volumes could not start OpenClaw with two valid agent directories whose names differ only by case. Startup incorrectly treated the paths as the same directory based on the host OS instead of the target volume's filesystem semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent-directory collision identity now follows the target filesystem. Existing paths and their nearest existing parents are realpath-normalized, while the shared path-case probe determines whether case folding is appropriate without creating configured directories. The same probe remains the canonical implementation for trusted safe-bin paths.

This preserves rejection for true duplicates, case aliases on case-insensitive volumes, and symlink aliases, while allowing genuinely distinct directories on case-sensitive volumes.

## User Impact

Multi-agent configurations can use case-distinct state directories on case-sensitive APFS/NTFS volumes without being rejected at startup. Existing protections against agents sharing the same auth and session state remain in place.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test that runs the macOS comparison branch against a case-sensitive filesystem and verifies case-distinct directories remain separate.
- Added coverage proving symlink aliases still resolve to one duplicate agent directory.
- Created and mounted a real case-sensitive APFS image on macOS and verified existing case-distinct directories, missing paths under an empty mount root, and numeric-only leaf names all report `caseInsensitive: false` without leaving probe entries.
- Verified an empty directory on the default case-insensitive macOS volume reports `caseInsensitive: true` and remains empty after probing.
- Verified a caller spelling such as `Foo` still resolves case-insensitively when the stored directory entry uses another spelling such as `fOO`.
- `oxfmt 0.58.0` completed successfully for all four changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The final repository autoreview completed cleanly with Codex CLI 0.144.1, `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning, branch mode against `main`, and no web search. Earlier review rounds found four filesystem identity edge cases; all were accepted, fixed, and included in the clean final review.
- Path-scoped pull-request CI is pending and will run when this draft is marked ready for review.
